revisions.html:
Experience different interaction models

UI approaches are different instruments

Each station gives you a small real task with a matching interaction style. Switch stations, act inside them, and your choices become a trail for the next evolution of this workspace.

Act, then the work develops

Your trail

Meaningful actions are saved here. This makes the lab less like a slide deck and more like a workspace that can respond to your taste.

Compare by feel

  • Direct manipulation uses eye, hand, and immediate spatial feedback.
  • Guided flow narrows choices to reduce errors.
  • Commands favor terse expression and repeatable operations.
  • Facets support exploration without knowing exact words.
  • Simulation exposes tradeoffs by continuous adjustment.
  • Rule building lets you construct behavior rather than request it once.

Experience different interaction models

UI approaches are instruments

Switch stations, act inside them, and compare how each approach changes what feels easy: moving, choosing, commanding, filtering, tuning, or constructing behavior.

Responsive: trail stacks before overlap

Your trail

Meaningful actions are saved here so the lab can evolve from what you actually try.

Compare by feel
  • Direct manipulation: eye, hand, immediate spatial feedback.
  • Guided flow: safe order and fewer missed steps.
  • Commands: terse, repeatable operations.
  • Facets: exploration without exact keywords.
  • Simulation: visible tradeoffs.
  • Rules: durable behavior you assemble.
